# 00. Zero-based operating economics: direct answers

**Status:** research only. No production implementation, paid research, outreach or expenditure is authorised, and nothing here authorises any.

**Sources and review.** Every figure below is generated by the F# model in [`model/`](model/) from [`data/inputs/`](data/inputs/):
- Generated tables: [`data/outputs/results.md`](data/outputs/results.md).
- Prices: 268 public price points checked on 2026-11-27 ([evidence](data/evidence/)).
- Obligations: the Unbound requirements ([extract](data/evidence/architecture-obligations.md)).
- Review: three independent adversarial reviewers raised 79 findings. 33 were accepted, 34 partially accepted and 12 rejected ([11](11-adversarial-review.md)).

**How to read the numbers**
- **Cash** means new cash Echelon Foundry spends in a year. It assumes the founder works up to 1,200 h a year on the DAF business without pay (range 800–1,800 h). The noncash value of those hours is shown separately at $123/h.
- **Base** is the all-most-likely case. Because the cost ranges are right-skewed, base sits below the Monte Carlo median. Where it matters, the median (P50) and P90 are shown too.
- Unless stated otherwise:
  - the commercial model is technology licensing (L);
  - customers arrive in a mixed order of institution sizes, and the first is a mid-size community foundation (300 accounts, about $60M of assets);
  - contracts are typical institutional contracts (tier 1).

| # | Question | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **What does it cost to keep Unbound running with no customers?** | **About $7k a year in cash; median about $24k, P90 about $70k.** Infrastructure is about $5k: a managed PostgreSQL cluster with a standby, two app containers, write-once storage, WAF/DNS, keys and staging. The founder carries about 1,180 h of keep-qualified work: patching, dependency upgrades, the IRS/OFAC data archive and management. Those hours are worth about $145k. **If the founder were paid market rate, the cost would be about $152k a year.** The fully loaded cost, including the amortised build, is about $361k. In the median case the founder is short of hours and some engineering is contracted. |
| 2 | **What does it cost to support the first paying customer?** | **Licensing: about $200k a year in cash at run-rate (median $275k, P90 $345–420k). Full-service administration: about $325k (median $410k).** The first customer triggers three things:<br>• Assurance and insurance, about $55k: SOC 2 Type II, pen test, compliance platform, E&O/cyber at $2M, counsel and endpoint protection.<br>• An independent reviewer retainer for non-author change approval: $12k.<br>• Above all, a second engineer, contracted at about 870 h a year. Unbound's two-person controls (two-deep on-call, two-person break-glass) need that second qualified person, and the founder's hours run out.<br>**Before the first invoice**, a one-off go-live amount of about $170k falls in year 0: onboarding and hypercare (about 340 h), acquisition, prepaid assurance and insurance, and six months of the first-customer run-rate while SOC 2 observation and coverage start ([10](10-sensitivity.md)). |
| 3 | **What is the marginal cost of each additional customer?** | **Licensing: about $37k a year in cash for a customer of average mixed size (median $47k), or about $30–40 per account.** The first customers cost more because each brings step costs (insurance, SOC scope, coverage).<br>**Full-service administration: about $90–120k per customer**, because Echelon Foundry prepares exceptions, closes and reconciliations.<br>**Charity intelligence subscriptions: about $1k each.**<br>The sponsor carries its own reserved decisions and rail fees in every model, about $90k a year for an average sponsor ([06](06-institutional-growth-scenarios.md)). |
| 4 | **At what point must we hire someone?** | **A second qualified engineer is needed from the first customer**, because of Unbound's two-person controls and the founder's limited hours. At first that person can be a contractor.<br>**An employee becomes cheaper than contracting at about 5 licensing customers in the base case.** In the median draw it happens at the first customer, because platform maintenance and founder hours are the two largest uncertainties. With full-service administration, the first operations employee comes at about 4 customers, or at the first customer if that customer is large. The founder's own management, sales and account-management load needs a first hire at about 25 customers under licensing or full service ([05](05-staffing-derivation.md)). |
| 5 | **Which obligations cannot be automated?** | **Decisions reserved to the sponsor:** grant exceptions, ambiguous charity eligibility, payment release under dual control, monthly reconciliation sign-off, OFAC blocking and reporting, successor approval, gift acceptance and board policy adoption. Law and Unbound's requirements reserve these to accountable sponsor officials (IRC 4966(d)(2); CNV-GRT-001; CNV-GOV-003/004).<br>**Distinct people on Echelon Foundry's side:**<br>• two non-author approvers for control-module changes (CNV-PLT-010);<br>• two-person break-glass;<br>• an incident commander with a backup.<br>**External assurance:** SOC 2 and, for staffed administration, SOC 1 Type II.<br>**Contracting and counsel.**<br>Everything else is prevented, done deterministically or AI-assisted with a human checking exceptions ([04](04-human-intervention-challenge.md)). |
| 6 | **What costs belong to the sponsor rather than Echelon Foundry?** | Unbound never holds money (CNV-LEG-001), so the following belong to the sponsor in every model:<br>• its reserved decisions;<br>• payment-rail fees (ACH, check and wire; about $0.50 per transaction);<br>• its own financial audit;<br>• sponsor-side migration work;<br>• positive pay.<br>Under licensing it also performs its own exception handling and reconciliation. That totals about $90k a year for an average mixed-size sponsor under licensing, and about $39k under full service. Echelon Foundry may not be the sponsor, the Originator or the operator (UNB-CDD-CMF-005). |
| 7 | **What is the minimum credible licensing price?** | **About $45–60k a year for an average mixed-size customer (about 1,200 accounts), or about $40–55 per account.** That is cash break-even at 10–25 customers ($44–57k per customer). It is not a price at which any single customer can be served profitably from day one.<br>**Floor:** never below marginal cost, about $37k per customer or about $30 per account.<br>**Below about 10 customers no price is credible for a 300-account foundation.** Cost per customer is $117k at 2 customers and $77k at 5. That is why channel or anchor customers matter.<br>**At the fully loaded cost** (founder at market rate, build amortised over 5 years) the floor is $58–92k per customer ($53–78 per account) at 10–25 customers. Ren's ~$81 per account is the market comparator. |
| 8 | **What is the minimum credible administration fee?** | **About 10–15 bps on a portfolio of at least about $0.7B; 5 bps never breaks even.** Full-service cash cost is about 7 bps of assets at 10–25 customers (median 9 bps, P90 10–13 bps), and 9–15 bps fully loaded.<br>**Persistent cash break-even:**<br>• at 10 bps: 5 customers ($0.67B);<br>• at 15–20 bps: 2 customers ($0.33B);<br>• at 5 bps: never within 400 customers.<br>**A single customer needs about $162M of assets at 20 bps** ($360M fully loaded), or $360M at 10 bps.<br>**Constraints:**<br>• Unbound requires no Unbound staff in sponsor workflows at release 1 (UNB-CDD-CMF-002), so full service is not a release-1 offer.<br>• It also needs SOC 1 Type II readiness before the first staffed client (CNV-GOV-001). |
| 9 | **Can the first customer finance subsequent growth?** | **Only if the first customer is large, or the model is full service at 15 bps or more.**<br>**Licensing:**<br>• A 300-account foundation loses about $166k a year as the only customer.<br>• Licensing stays in deficit until about 7 mixed-size customers.<br>• A first customer of regional scale (6,000 accounts, $720M) is cash-positive from day one (+$59k a year).<br>**Full service at 20 bps:**<br>• Positive from the second customer (two customers, $330M).<br>• An all-small-foundation book needs 5 customers.<br>**Not self-financing at reference prices:**<br>• White-label and limited-operations licensing do not self-finance at the tested reference prices for typical sponsors.<br>• Charity intelligence needs about 30 subscribers.<br>**Migration services** self-finance per project ([06](06-institutional-growth-scenarios.md), [07](07-commercial-models.md)). |
| 10 | **Is external capital actually necessary?** | **Not for the anchor-first or full-service routes; probably yes for licensing to small foundations.**<br>**Common to all routes:**<br>• Cash cost of the build: about $108k ($47–230k) for independent review, pen test, SOC 2 Type I, CPA ledger review, counsel and rehearsal.<br>• The real cost of the build is about **7,560 founder hours** ($1.04M fully loaded). That is over six years at 1,200 h a year, so time, not cash, is the binding constraint.<br>**Deepest cumulative cash deficit after production qualification, adding two customers a year (base):**<br>• licensing with an anchor first: about $0.20M;<br>• full service at 20 bps: about $0.28M;<br>• licensing to mixed sponsors: about $0.76M, self-sustaining at 8 customers in year 4;<br>• licensing to mid-size foundations only: about $1.3M;<br>• small foundations only: about $2.4M.<br>**If inputs are adverse, no route becomes self-sustaining within 15 years.**<br>**Conclusion:** if the founder can fund about $0.3M and keep contributing unpaid time, an anchor-first or channel-led route needs no external capital. A direct route to small sponsors does ([10](10-sensitivity.md)). |

| Prior estimate | Phase II | Zero-based (base; favourable–adverse) | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Administration fixed cost | $2.5M per year (total with variable at 10k accounts: $3.97M) | $0.94M total cash ($0.20M–4.2M) at 5 × 2,000 accounts; $1.29M fully loaded | Lower |
| Licensing fixed cost | $1.8M per year (total: $2.11M) | $0.39M total cash ($0.08M–1.6M); $0.75M fully loaded | Lower |
| Variable cost per account | $147 | $64 slope ($15–326); $94 including sponsor-borne work | Lower; wide |
| Charity registry | $90–170k | $89k ($22k–476k) | Same |
| Customer acquisition | $125k | $37k ($14k–97k), mostly founder time | Lower |
| Development | $1.94M | $108k cash plus 7,560 founder hours ($1.04M fully loaded; $0.43M–2.33M) | Cash much lower; economic cost about half, and time-bound |
| Commercial validation | $150–350k | $15k cash; $113k fully loaded | Lower |
| Partner pilot (cumulative) | $1.0–1.5M | $0.89M including build cash ($0.08M–never recovers) | Similar in the base case |

Detail and reasoning: [08](08-prior-estimate-challenges.md).

## What would change these answers
- **Measured platform maintenance and founder availability.** These are the two largest drivers of first-customer cost (±$80k each), and the reason the median hires at the first customer.
- **The size of the first customer.** It determines whether growth self-finances.
- **Exception intensity under full service.** This drives the fee per customer. The touch rates are unmeasured ([12](12-evidence-gaps.md)).
- **Whether change-driven re-vetting holds (OD-CDD-02).** If the 180-day reviews revert to manual and Echelon Foundry performs them, licensing cost at 10 customers rises from $0.57M to $0.78M. Who performs the residual reviews (P3-DEC-MOD005) matters little ([06](06-institutional-growth-scenarios.md)).
